_comment: A Vita project is one game, the licence a packaged one needs, and whatever the game already saved. The system software is firmware (the System Software setting says which).

slots.title: Game
slots.help: The game: a .vpk, a NoNpDRM dump as a .zip (the game's folder with its sce_sys/package/work.bin), or the PlayStation Store's own package, a .pkg, with the game's licence in the Licence slot. Vita3K installs it into the machine before it starts. Vita3K's compatibility list (vita3k.org/compatibility) says which games work.

slots.title: Licence
slots.help: The licence a .pkg game is decrypted with: its work.bin (the 512-byte file a NoNpDRM dump keeps in sce_sys/package), or the console's own .rif for the game. A package is encrypted and installs nothing without it; a .vpk or a .zip dump needs none, because a dump carries its own. It is pinned by hash like the game, and the movie cites it.

slots.title: Save data
slots.help: What the game already saved, as Emulator > Export Save Data... wrote it: a .zip with savedata/<TITLE ID>/... (the save data system's) and data/... (where homebrew keeps its). A save copied off a Vita with ux0:/user/00/ in front, or a bare <TITLE ID>/ folder, is taken too. It goes into the machine before the game starts.
